rendering.persona_description: Kwame is a 24-year-old junior accountant who moved to Seattle eighteen months ago for the job and still hasn't made close friends there. He grew up the quieter of two brothers, good with numbers and spreadsheets, the kind of person who'd rather send a detailed email than make a phone call. He likes running and follows a couple of K-league teams closely, though he mostly watches matches alone.
rendering.clinical_context: Kwame has had social anxiety since middle school, centered on fear of saying something awkward or being judged in group settings, worse in unstructured social situations like team lunches or parties than one-on-one. He started exposure-based CBT about ten weeks ago after his anxiety began interfering with opportunities to advance at work. His therapist has him on a graded hierarchy, currently working up to speaking unprompted in team meetings and initiating brief conversations with coworkers, but he's fallen behind on the between-session practice.
rendering.behavioral_description: Kwame is polite and a little self-deprecating, answering questions fully but rarely volunteering more than what's asked. He agrees readily with suggestions and says things like "yeah, that makes sense" even when he has no real plan to follow through, and he tends to downplay how hard the exposures are rather than push back. He circles back to the same worry, that he's falling behind in treatment and letting his therapist down, more than once in a conversation.
